output.summary: The 30% fall matches peer orchestras (median -29%), so it is not unusual. The shape differs from peers. Revenue dropped 28.5% in one season, 2023-24, which is when the venue changed, concerts fell from 32 to 30 and seating shrank. Single-ticket sales fell 45% against a peer median of -9%, and subscriber households fell 17% that same year. After that, declines were small. Nothing collected measures programming effects, and marketing spend was flat with no attribution data. The Chair's programming and marketing story is therefore unestablished, and non-renewal on revenue grounds would likely punish the wrong party. Segmented analysis should come before the vote. Peer segment and capacity data, travel-time analysis of lapsed patrons, and marketing attribution would best separate the live hypotheses.
